reason: The graph refresh is a recurring chore with non-obvious commit scope: backups and the .sig file must stay out, and there is no macOS timeout. No existing skill covers Eventar's graph commit. Project-level because the paths and the self-loop baseline are this repo's.
The episode's refresh step failed because `git add` aborted on an already-deleted path, and a code-only AST update nearly marked changed docs as seen. Both steps belong in the refresh runbook.

Refresh run exposed four gaps: compressed doc reads produced garbled nodes, bad nodes were hand-patched in graph.json, the report lost its Graph Freshness section, and the code-map-versus-state scope split was stated by Ivan but not in the skill.

On the 2026-11-14 MVP-close refresh, changed docs were re-extracted; the extraction prompt had to pin existing ids and the boundary-edge count was needed to avoid orphaning cross-doc edges. This procedure is absent from the skill.

Vault Decisions Log cannot be re-extracted whole; carry-over by source_file with count checks is the working method. Vault graph has no Graph Freshness section, which conflicts with step 9 as written.
A chunk agent died on a rate limit after writing a complete file; the rule as written would have aborted a usable chunk, and the merge-base and manifest-order rules were missing.

The 2026-11-17 B9 Stage 1 wrap-up ran a bare graph update, saw INFERRED edges collapse from 873 to 87, and switched to an AST-only merge. The skill gives no warning, so the next refresh can repeat the loss.

On 2026-11-17 the vault graph got a link to a new B9 note appended straight into graph.json, followed by graphify cluster-only. Step 8 already forbids hand-patching graph.json, so the skill needs to say appended links count too.

The handoff Closing line claimed "vault graph done" after a hand-written merge that added four nodes and an edge by script and did not re-extract the changed MVP Close note. CLAUDE.md says never claim a step that did not run, so the vault step needs an explicit partial state.

Episode hit a multiprocessing spawn crash when the code-only AST merge ran from a heredoc; the fix (write a script file with a __main__ guard) worked on the second try. Rule belongs in the graph-refresh skill that governs this step.
Regenerating the report dropped the Graph Freshness section again; the episode re-inserted it by hand. Step 9 names the check but not the fix, so the next refresh repeats the miss.
Absorbed into the Eventar card git workflow umbrella as the graph refresh commits subsection.
